EdPay · Shop Billing

Three ways to sell, one debit note — counter POS, a handheld terminal and online pre-orders for school stores, all posting to the same ledger.

Year2025 – 2026
ClientJDO Group
RoleProduct Designer
PlatformiPad POS · Handheld · Web · Mobile

The ecosystem

EdPay is a school payments ecosystem. Shop Billing is its retail side: a school store sells at the counter on an iPad POS, from a handheld terminal and through online pre-orders — and every payment ends up in the same debit note ledger that handles receivables and invoicing.

Built for school stores. Also works for general retail and F&B.

In numbers

3sales channels
4surfaces
42screens & states
5 → 3accounting steps per payment (internal figure from the product team)

Selling was quick. Bookkeeping lagged behind.

Three things slowed the store down after the sale. Each one maps to a part of the product.

BeforeAfter
Counter sales, online orders and payments were kept in separate places and reconciled at the end of the day.POS, handheld and pre-orders share one order queue and post to the same ledger.
Online payments passed through a third-party gateway before reaching the merchant.jLink replaces the gateway; funds settle in the merchant’s bank account.
Accountants created receivables, sent reminders and issued invoices by hand for each payment.The debit note system handles receivables, reminders, instalments and e-invoices.

What I designed

  • Counter POS (iPad) — the catalog follows the store’s product categories and the cart stays pinned to the right. Quick-tender amounts and change, receipt or e-invoice, and a shift close that compares drawer cash with the system total.
  • POS terminal (handheld) — the same flow for serving customers away from the counter or when the queue is long, so there is nothing new to learn.
  • Pre-order, in-store pickup — parents browse and pay online, or pay at the counter on pickup. The order lands in the cashier’s queue with its pickup time; guests track it with an order code, no account needed.
  • jLink payment page — amount, merchant and a session countdown stay at the top; a data policy checkbox gates confirm; six-digit OTP with resend after 60 seconds.
  • Also in EdPay — the jWallet student app (sign-up, top-up, transfers, spending limits, NFC tap-to-pay at campus POS) and the school admin portal for student, parent and card management.

Design choices

  • One queue for every channel. Walk-in sales and online pre-orders appear in the same order queue, so the cashier never checks two places.
  • Nothing new to learn. The handheld mirrors the iPad flow step for step.
  • Pay now or at pickup. Payment status and order progress sit side by side, so parents know when to come.
  • Money needs certainty. Every payment ends on a screen with amount, status and reference — nothing is “probably sent”.

Under the hood

Whichever channel makes the sale, the transaction lands in the debit note system: a receivable for each sale, reminders when a payment is due, instalments, e-invoices issued once a payment is confirmed, and direct settlement to the merchant’s bank account with partner banks.

The debit note system is a proprietary product and its UI is not shown here — see edpay.vn. How jLink works technically is under NDA.
